title: Reverse Words Using Recursion
statement:
You are given a sentence: words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing spaces. Print the sentence with the **order of the words reversed**. The letters inside each word keep their original order.

For example, `I love india` becomes `india love I`.

**Follow-up:** the original question asked for a recursive solution (no loops over the words). Try to write it recursively: reverse the rest of the sentence after the first word, then append that first word. This cannot be tested here, so the tests only check the output.
inputFormat: A single line containing the sentence.
outputFormat: Print the sentence with its words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.
constraints: 1 ≤ number of words ≤ 5000 (so a recursive solution stays within the recursion limit)
Words consist of letters and digits and are separated by exactly one space

examples.explanation: The three words appear in reverse order; each word itself is unchanged.
A single word stays the same.
The last word becomes first, and so on.

tests.input: P0unEd 2YFfjc Gne Bf oOQHn dc 99 V
tests.output: V 99 dc oOQHn Bf Gne 2YFfjc P0unEd

tests.input: nb bHmeUXO IJj3wl h 624OlD X5FKk a0S xrqQCR
tests.output: xrqQCR a0S X5FKk 624OlD h IJj3wl bHmeUXO nb

hints: Split the sentence into words first; the problem becomes reversing a list of words.
Recursive view: reverse(words) = reverse(words[1:]) followed by words[0]. The base case is an empty list.
If recursion feels heavy, an index-based two-pointer swap or a reversed join gives the same answer in O(n).
